svg.text: Pre-eclampsia: the disease is in the whole body, not the blood pressure
Delivery is the only cure. Everything else buys time safely.
Signs that the disease is severe
Headache that will not clear with paracetamol
Blurred vision or flashing lights
Pain under the ribs on the right side
Vomiting late in pregnancy
Reduced urine output, brisk reflexes
These are brain, liver and kidney — not symptoms of anxiety
What the nurse does while waiting
Quiet room, side-lying, never left alone
Magnesium sulphate to prevent the fit
Antihypertensive to protect her brain vessels
Strict fluid balance — over-loading floods the lungs
Prepare for delivery: it is the treatment
Lowering the pressure does not cure the disease
Magnesium sulphate: three checks before every maintenance dose
1. Knee jerk present — reflexes disappear first, and that is the earliest warning
2. Respiratory rate above 16 per minute — breathing slows next
3. Urine output at least 100 mL in the last 4 hours — the drug leaves only by the kidney
Antidote: calcium gluconate, kept at the bedside, not in the cupboard
During a fit
Do not restrain her and do not force
anything into her mouth
Protect her head, turn her on her side
when it ends, then oxygen and suction
It does not end at delivery
Fits still occur after the baby is born, so
magnesium continues for 24 hours after
delivery or the last fit, whichever is later.
The postnatal ward is where she is forgotten.
